title: Rank-one R_z T-duals of compact three-dimensional almost abelian solvmanifolds are Morita-equivalent noncommutative two-torus bundles over the Mostow circle
author: Paolo Aschieri; Richard J. Szabo
difficulty_reason: The proof explicitly parameterizes the right-action cosets and reconstructs the induced lattice translations before decomposing the crossed product. It constructs an equivariant imprimitivity module to identify the nonsingular fibers with noncommutative two-tori and treats the exceptional zero-denominator fibers separately. The monodromy is then transported to a fractional-linear action and a Morita equivalence, supplying the geometric fiber description rather than only invoking abstract T-duality.
source_version: Official SIGMA 17 (2021) article 012, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2021.012; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Select Theorem4.17 with d=3 and the R_z action specified in Section4.6: G=R2 semidirect_phi R has a cocompact lattice Lambda, z0 is the lattice-rational chosen nontrivial torsion-direction vector in image(phi_x0-id), and R_z0 intersect Lambda is a lattice. The Mostow circle, period matrix Sigma and lattice monodromy conventions4.2–4.4 are retained. The full author coset, lattice-action, fiber crossed-product and equivariant Morita-module computations4.16–4.17 are present;4.18/4.19 supply the monodromy interpretation. Existing Green imprimitivity, semidirect crossed-product decomposition and noncommutative-torus Morita facts are genuinely prior background. The conclusion is Morita equivalence, not isomorphism of the original crossed product to a commutative space, and the exceptional fibers are treated as in the source. Higher-dimensional and separate classical H-flux branches are contextual only.

statement_scope: Theorem4.17 with d=3 and precisely the lattice-rational R_z action of Section4.6. Full local author proof and monodromy supports included; no higher-dimensional claim or separate classical-circle T-dual theorem.
